--- .opencode/plans/ci-green-pr7-pr8.md

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# Plan: Make PR #7 and PR #8 CI green
+
+Both PRs in alehar9320/agentic-odi have failing CI. Fix root causes with real
+fixes (tests first), verify locally mirroring CI, push, watch checks.
+
+Global constraints:
+- Never weaken security scanning to get green (no bandit config skips).
+- Mirror CI commands exactly for local verification.
+- Work only in the two existing worktrees:
+  - PR #8: .worktrees/cli-bundled-distribution (feature/cli-bundled-distribution)
+  - PR #7: .worktrees/living-studio-tauri (topic/living-studio-tauri)
+- No rebase needed (both MERGEABLE on current origin/main).
+
+## Root causes (evidence verified)
+
+### PR #8 — security job (then CI green; smoke skipped, never ran)
+Bandit, 6 issues in cli/src:
+1. B110 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:42-43 — `except Exception: pass` in `_startup_auto_update`
+2. B606 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:78 — `os.execv` re-exec of own binary
+3. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:79 — `zf.extractall(dest)` (bandit flags any
+   `extractall` when the module also imports `tarfile`; CPython `_extract_member`
+   strips `..`/absolute paths — verified in stdlib source)
+4. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:82 — `tf.extractall(dest)` unvalidated
+5. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:168 — `urlopen` (`# noqa: S310` affects neither ruff nor bandit)
+6. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:173 — same
+All other scanned srcs clean. Bandit accepts literal `filter="data"` kwarg
+(verified in bandit 1.9.4 plugin source: returns None → no issue).
+All URLs derive from https constants (RELEASES_API, _RELEASES_DOWNLOAD).
+
+### PR #7 — studio + tauri-build + smoke (then CI green)
+1. TS2307 `Cannot find module '../../lib/odi'` — `studio/src/lib/{odi.ts,odi.test.ts}`
+   exist on disk but were never committed: root `.gitignore` unanchored `lib/`
+   (stock Python template) swallows any dir named lib. Verified: root `lib/` never
+   existed in history, no script writes it, all Python pkgs use src/ layout,
+   venv libs covered by `.venv/`/`venv/`/`env/`.
+2. Smoke sidecar probe 422s: POST `/api/health/mcp` with `{}` but
+   `McpHealthRequest.mcp_url` is required; GET `/api/canvas` missing required
+   `mcp_url` query. Both curl legs fail (verified in run log + router.py + tests).
+3. Steps never reached after early failures: studio unit tests/build/gen-check,
+   client.run smoke step — must de-risk locally.
+Decision (user-approved evaluation): anchor `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`;
+keep the canonical `studio/src/lib` name (industry-standard TS source dir).
+
+## Task 1: PR #8 — failing tests first
+- Worktree cli-bundled-distribution. In cli/tests/test_update.py add:
+  - `test_extract_archive_rejects_tar_path_traversal`: tar with member
+    `../escape.txt` → `extract_archive` must raise and no file may appear outside dest.
+    RED now (extractall without filter writes outside).
+  - `test_extract_archive_contains_zip_path_traversal`: zip member `../evil.txt`
+    → extracted only under dest, no escape (documents zipfile sanitization).
+  - `test_default_fetch_rejects_non_https`: `update._default_fetch("file:///<tmp>")`
+    → raises `update.UpdateError` and does not return file content. RED now.
+Expected: pytest shows the two RED tests failing for the right reasons.
+
+## Task 2: PR #8 — real fixes
+- update.py `extract_archive`: tar branch → `tf.extractall(dest, filter="data")`;
+  zip branch → keep + `# nosec B202 - ZipFile._extract_member strips absolute/'..' paths`.
+- update.py: add `_require_https(url)` (raise `UpdateError` unless scheme == "https"),
+  call from `_default_fetch` and `_default_fetch_bytes`; replace `# noqa: S310` with
+  `# nosec B310 - scheme enforced by _require_https`.
+- cli.py: `pass` → `return None` (keep `# noqa: BLE001`).
+- cli.py:78: trailing `# nosec B606` + justification (re-execs own verified binary).
+Expected: new tests GREEN; full cli suite GREEN.
+
+## Task 3: PR #8 — local CI mirror + smoke de-risk
+- `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src` → exit 0
+- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` → clean
+- mypy: `uv run --directory <pkg> mypy .` for core, mcp_server, local_server, cli, client, connectors
+- `uv run --directory cli pytest` → all pass
+- Smoke steps (never ran on this PR): `uv run python -m cli --version`;
+  `uv run python -m cli connectors --help` greps for list+ingest;
+  MCP server boot probe on :8000 (verbatim from ci.yml); client.run probe (verbatim).
+
+## Task 4: PR #8 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit with repo-style message; push; `gh pr checks 8 --watch`.
+
+## Task 5: PR #7 — gitignore + track src/lib
+- Worktree living-studio-tauri. Root `.gitignore`: `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`.
+- `git add studio/src/lib` (odi.ts, odi.test.ts); confirm nothing else newly unignored
+  (`git status --short` shows only intended files).
+
+## Task 6: PR #7 — fix smoke probe 422s
+- ci.yml sidecar probe:
+  - `-d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}'`
+  - `http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`
+- Expected: both legs 200 (health returns reachable=false when MCP down; canvas
+  falls back to seed payload — verified in probes.py/mcp_data.py).
+
+## Task 7: PR #7 — local verification (incl. never-reached steps)
+- `cd studio && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run
+  && npm run build && npm run gen:api-types && git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts`
+- Run edited sidecar probe verbatim (sidecar via `uv run python -m local_server.main`).
+- Run client.run probe verbatim (never ran in CI).
+- tauri-build: frontend `npm run build` is the actual CI failure (covered above);
+  cargo side previously green in tauri-check; full `npm run tauri build` only if
+  system webkit deps available locally.
+
+## Task 8: PR #7 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit; push; `gh pr checks 7 --watch`.
+
+## Task 9: Final review
+- Review both diffs against plan; verification-before-completion before any
+  success claim; report rulings/deferreds.

+"""Tests for the CLI backend abstraction."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json

+from cli.backend import BackendConfig, LocalBackend, MCPBackend, resolve_backend
+
+
+def _id_from(text: str) -> str:
+    match = re.search(r"({.*})", text)
+    assert match is not None, text
+    return json.loads(match.group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[index]

+def test_local_backend_full_crud_round_trip(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=db)
+    job_text = backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J", "description": "d"})
+    assert "created successfully" in job_text
+    import json
+    import re
+
+    job_id = json.loads(re.search(r"({.*})", job_text).group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+    backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1})
+    backend.call(

+            "job_id": job_id,
+            "statement": "Min x",
+            "importance": 8.0,
+            "satisfaction": 4.0,

+    )
+    listed = backend.call("get_outcomes", {"job_id": job_id})
+    assert "Min x" in listed
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_jobs", {}))[0]["name"] == "J"
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_warns_on_db_with_mcp(capsys):
+    resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="mcp", db_path="x.db", mcp_url="http://x/mcp"))
+    assert "ignored" in capsys.readouterr().err.lower()
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_unknown_raises():
+    import pytest
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="nope", db_path=None, mcp_url=None))
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_returns_matching_backend_types(tmp_path):
+    local = resolve_backend(
+        BackendConfig(backend="local", db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"), mcp_url=None)
+    )
+    assert isinstance(local, LocalBackend)
+    mcp = resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="mcp", db_path=None, mcp_url="http://x/mcp"))
+    assert isinstance(mcp, MCPBackend)
+
+
+def test_local_backend_job_step_outcome_lifecycle(tmp_path):
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

+

+
+    step_id = _id_from(backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1}))
+    job_map = backend.call("get_job_map", {"job_id": job_id})
+    assert json.loads(job_map)[0]["name"] == "S"
+    assert "Step updated successfully" in backend.call(

+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_step", {"step_id": step_id}))["name"] == "S2"
+
+    outcome_id = _id_from(

+    )
+    assert "Outcome updated successfully" in backend.call(

+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id}))["importance"] == 9.0
+
+    assert "Step deleted successfully" in backend.call("delete_step", {"step_id": step_id})
+    assert "Outcome deleted successfully" in backend.call(

+    assert "Job deleted successfully" in backend.call("delete_job", {"job_id": job_id})

+    )

+        == range_error
+    )

+    assert data["customer_value"]["value_metrics"][0]["name"] == "m2"

This choice determines the hero, the entire conversion flow, and which of the doc's seven sections is the terminal action — it's the single load-bearing decision on the page. Related sub-question I also can't check without credentials: does the hosted instance have representative seeded ODI data, or would a new visitor land in an empty demo?

**2. What channel should the site present for obtaining access, and is publishing that channel approved?**

README says only "reach out to the maintainers." The page needs a concrete, clickable path (GitHub Issues enabled? Discussions? email address? Discord? calendly?). Wrong guess matters twice: no channel = dead-end conversion (violates the "one obvious CTA" goal), and publishing a personal email or a channel that isn't actually monitored is worse than none. This shapes the hero's supporting microcopy, section 6 ("Honest status"), and the footer.

Section 5 ("For builders") wants an MCP endpoint snippet, but nothing in the repo documents the auth mechanism for `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp` (no bearer/header/env-var convention anywhere in code or docs — the only `API_KEY` reference is the unrelated local LLM key in `client/src/client/app.py`). Different answers change section 5's content and whether it demonstrates value to the "AI/agent developers" audience or just the install one-liner.

**4. Is a committed PNG binary acceptable for the OG/Twitter card, and if so, who generates it — a script run by you, or the deploy workflow?**

Wrong guess in either direction undercuts the credibility the page is built on, and the two answers imply very different amounts of investigation into `app.py` before designing the SVG/CSS.

**7. What is the approved citation target for the ~86% ODI success-rate claim?**

This changes the markup of the one stat callout on the page, and it's a legal-adjacent call I shouldn't make unilaterally.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** On first interactive launch, the CLI captures a PM baseline via URL auto-detect with typed fallback, persists it to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json`, and exposes `setup`/`profile` commands; the first-run hook never fires again once the file exists.

**Architecture:** Three new modules in the `cli` package: `profile.py` (baseline model, XDG config path, atomic load/save, `setup`/`profile` Typer sub-app), `infer.py` (deterministic keyword-based domain/business-model inference from page text), `onboard.py` (httpx fetch + stdlib HTML signal extraction, confirmation card, typed fallback, first-run hook). The hook is wired into the existing root Typer callback in `cli.py`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Typer, httpx (new declared `cli` dependency), stdlib `html.parser`, pytest, uv.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-first-run-onboarding-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Python `>= 3.10`; CLI package `agentic-odi-cli`, entry `cli.cli:app`.
- Config dir: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi` → `~/.config/agentic-odi` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\agentic-odi`); baseline file `baseline.json`.
- All user-facing copy renders the invoked program name via `Path(sys.argv[0]).name` (helper `cli.cli_name()`), never a hard-coded `odi`/`agentic-odi`.
- No LLM calls, no network in tests (httpx `MockTransport` only), no writes outside the XDG config dir (tests override `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `HOME` via monkeypatch + tmp_path).
- Schema: only `schema_version` is required; all other fields may be `null`/empty; confirmation card renders only non-null lines. JSON keys are **flat** (`product_name`, `product_url`) rather than the spec's nested `product` object — simpler for the dataclass round-trip (builder call).
- `--version` needs no guard in the hook: the eager Typer option callback raises `Exit` during parsing, before the root callback body runs.

(Task 3) 2. **Non-interactive first run (CI, pipes)** — one hint line, command continues, never blocks. (Task 5) 3. **Confidently wrong inference** — card always shown; nothing written to disk before the user confirms. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): 108: 109: ```bash 110: # Add a Customer Outcome 111: agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" 112: 113: # List outcomes (optionally filtered) 114: agentic-odi outcomes list 115: agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id 116: 117: # Get, update, delete 118: agentic-odi outcomes get 119: agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 120: agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes 121: 122: # Compute ODI Opportunity Score 123: agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 124: ``` 125: 126: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. 127: 128: ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP Ingest) 129: 130: Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and 171: - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. 172: 173: A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 174: 175: 1. **Install a local LLM server** 176: 177: Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): 178: 179: ```bash 180: pip install llama-cpp-python 181: ``` 182: 183: 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** 184: 185: Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 186: 187: 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** 188: 189: Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`): 190: 191: ```bash 192: python -m llama_cpp.server \ 193: --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ 194: --model_alias local-tools-model \ 195: --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ 196: --chat_format openai 197: ``` 198: 199: This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 200: 201: 4. **Configure the Streamlit client** 202: 203: `client/src/client/app.py` reads the following environment variables (with sensible defaults): 204: 205: | Variable | Default | 206: |---|---| 207: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | 208: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | 209: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | 210: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | 211: 212: You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **"LLM Configuration"**. 213: 214: 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** 215: 216: - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: 217: 218: ```bash 219: curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models 220: ``` 221: 222: If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. 223: 224: - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above). 225: - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository."* 226: - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. You can also trigger them manually with: 272: 273: ```bash 274: pre-commit run --all-files 275: ``` 276: 277: --- 278: 279: ## ✅ Testing 280: 281: Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: 282: 283: ```bash 284: uv run --directory core pytest 285: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest 286: uv run --directory local_server pytest 287: uv run --directory client pytest 288: uv run --directory cli pytest 289: uv run --directory connectors pytest 290: ``` 291: 292: ### 📊 Test Coverage Map 293: 294: | File | What it covers | 295: |---|---| 296: | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | 297: | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD | 298: | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | 299: | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | 300: | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | 301: | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | 302: | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | 303: | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) | 304: | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | 305: | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub | 306: | `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | CLI `connectors` add/list/health/ingest adapter | 307: | `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON connector registry persist/load and kind checks | 308: | `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | In-memory FastMCP health and ingest records | 309: 310: **Conventions:** 311: 312: - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. 313: - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. 314: - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. 315: - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. 316: 317: > [!TIP] 318: > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. 319: 320: ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking 321: 322: Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. 323: 324: --- 325: 326: ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi 327: 328: This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. 329: 330: To enable: 331: 332: 1. Start Pi: `pi` 335: 336: The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. 343: 344: ### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting 345: 346: - **When editing Python files**, either: 347: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or 348: - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: 349: 350: ```bash 351: uv run ruff format . 352: ``` 353: 354: - **CI behavior**: 355: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. 356: - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. 357: - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. 358: 359: --- 360: 361: ## ☁️ Deployment 362: 363: The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. 364: 365: ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) 366: 367: Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: 368: 369: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** 370: 371: ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint 372: 373: Integrate via the MCP protocol at: 374: 375: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** 376: 377: > [!IMPORTANT] 378: > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of **six** installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport). | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | **The Living Studio** — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation. Provides an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous conversational agent connected to the MCP server. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Studio UI together. | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides version/help plus `outcomes` and `connectors` commands. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode. ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal — no chat UI required. It provides version and help information plus commands for connecting to external systems. Over time it will also expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes). Launch it with: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # show help when no command is given ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi outcomes list agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi outcomes get agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes # Compute ODI Opportunity Score agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 ``` Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP Ingest) Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is `mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an external MCP **server**. ```bash python -m cli connectors add mcp --name gong --url http://localhost:9000/mcp --tool latest_quote python -m cli connectors list python -m cli connectors health --name gong python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong ``` Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are not written into the ODI jobs/outcomes store. ### ⚡ One-Command Launch (recommended) `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Studio UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both. ```bash python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio UI | http://localhost:8501 | ### 🔧 Manual Split-Terminal (alternative) Open two terminals and run each process separately: ```bash # Terminal 1 — MCP server python -m mcp_server # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI streamlit run client/src/client/app.py ``` ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`): ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server \ --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ --model_alias local-tools-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ --chat_format openai ``` This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 4. **Configure the Streamlit client** `client/src/client/app.py` reads the following environment variables (with sensible defaults): | Variable | Default | |---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **"LLM Configuration"**. 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models ``` If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above). - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository."* - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. ### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. --- ## 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: ```bash # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) uv run --directory core mypy . uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . uv run --directory local_server mypy . uv run --directory client mypy . uv run --directory cli mypy . uv run --directory connectors mypy . # Security scanning uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src # Tests (same as CI) uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv tool install pre-commit pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: ```bash pre-commit run --all-files ``` --- ## ✅ Testing Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: ```bash uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` ### 📊 Test Coverage Map | File | What it covers | |---|---| | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD | | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) | | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub | | `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | CLI `connectors` add/list/health/ingest adapter | | `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON connector registry persist/load and kind checks | | `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | In-memory FastMCP health and ingest records | **Conventions:** - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. > [!TIP] > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. --- ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. To enable: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve` 3. Start Pi: `pi` The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.) > [!NOTE] > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. ### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting - **When editing Python files**, either: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: ```bash uv run ruff format . ``` - **CI behavior**: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. --- ## ☁️ Deployment The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint Integrate via the MCP protocol at: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** > [!IMPORTANT] > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client. --- ## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include: - [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests. - [ ] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store. - [ ] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same `Connector` protocol. - [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*. - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path. - [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`. - [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data. - [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features. --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Please ensure any change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) before opening a pull request. --- ## 📄 License No license has been specified for this repository yet. <content>
1: # First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design
2: 
3: **Date:** 2026-10-16
4: **Status:** Approved
5: **Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile
6: 
7: ## Intent & Why
8: 
9: Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.
10: 
11: Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.
12: 
13: ## Goals
14: 
15: - First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
16: - Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
17: - Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
18: - Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
19: - `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
20: - PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).
21: 
22: ## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
23: 
24: - No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
25: - No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
26: - No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
27: - No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
28: - No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).
29: 
30: ## User Flow
31: 
32: ### 1. Trigger
33: 
34: - Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
35: - Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
36: - Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.
37: 
38: ### 2. Opening (the designed moment)
39: 
40: ```
41: Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.
42: 
43: Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
44: First: what product are you working on?
45: Paste a product URL or company name:
46: ```
47: 
48: ### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect
49: 
50: 1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
51: 2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
52: 3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
53: 4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
54: 5. Show the confirmation card:
55: 
56: ```
57: Based on sentry.io — does this look right?
58: 
59:   Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
60:   Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
61:   Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
62:   Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging
63: 
64:   [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
65: ```
66: 
67: 6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).
68: 
69: ### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)
70: 
71: Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):
72: 
73: 1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
74: 2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
75: 3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).
76: 
77: Then the same confirmation card and save.
78: 
79: ### 5. After onboarding
80: 
81: - Baseline file presence suppresses the hook forever.
82: - `odi setup` — full re-run, overwrites file (keeps a timestamped backup).
83: - `odi profile` — print the current card from the file. (`setup`/`profile` confirmed: plain language, matches the reserved `odi` alias.)
84: - All user-facing copy (hints, "Try: …" lines) uses the invoked program name (`sys.argv[0]` basename) so it is valid on any install, `odi` or `agentic-odi`.
85: - Skills/agent consumption (future): the file path is stable and documented; `odi profile --json` dumps machine-readable baseline.
86: 
87: ## Data Model
88: 
89: `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):
90: 
91: ```json
92: {
93:   "schema_version": 1,
94:   "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
95:   "source": "url" | "typed",
96:   "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
97:   "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
98:   "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
99:   "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
100:   "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
101:   "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
102:   "confidence": "high" | "low"
103: }
104: ```
105: 
106: Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.
107: 
108: ## Code Layout (new)
109: 
110: ```
111: cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
112: cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
113: cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
114: cli/tests/test_onboard.py
115: cli/tests/test_infer.py
116: cli/tests/test_profile.py
117: ```
118: 
119: - `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
120: - httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.
121: 
122: ## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)
123: 
124: - Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
125: - Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
126: - Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
127: - Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
128: - `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.
129: 
130: ## Constraints
131: 
132: - Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
133: - Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design

**Date:** 2026-10-16
**Status:** Approved
**Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile

## Intent & Why

Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.

Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.

## Goals

- First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
- Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
- Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
- Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
- `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
- PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
- No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
- No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
- No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
- No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).

## User Flow

### 1. Trigger

- Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
- Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
- Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.

### 2. Opening (the designed moment)

```
Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.

Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
First: what product are you working on?
Paste a product URL or company name:
```

### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect

1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
5. Show the confirmation card:

```
Based on sentry.io — does this look right?

  Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
  Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
  Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
  Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging

  [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
```

6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).

### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)

Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):

1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).

Then the same confirmation card and save.

### 5. After onboarding

- Baseline file presence suppresses the hook forever.
- `odi setup` — full re-run, overwrites file (keeps a timestamped backup).
- `odi profile` — print the current card from the file. (`setup`/`profile` confirmed: plain language, matches the reserved `odi` alias.)
- All user-facing copy (hints, "Try: …" lines) uses the invoked program name (`sys.argv[0]` basename) so it is valid on any install, `odi` or `agentic-odi`.
- Skills/agent consumption (future): the file path is stable and documented; `odi profile --json` dumps machine-readable baseline.

## Data Model

`~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "source": "url" | "typed",
  "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
  "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
  "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
  "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
  "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
  "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
  "confidence": "high" | "low"
}
```

Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.

## Code Layout (new)

```
cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
cli/tests/test_onboard.py
cli/tests/test_infer.py
cli/tests/test_profile.py
```

- `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
- httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.

## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)

- Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
- Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
- Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
- Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
- `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.

## Constraints

- Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
- Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.

## Review Focus (likely to bite)

1. Fetch hang/timeout on weird sites — hard 8s timeout, errors → typed path.
2. TTY detection wrong in some terminals — conservative check; hint-line behavior in non-TTY.
3. Inference confidently wrong — confirmation card always shown; nothing saved without confirm.
4. Concurrent first runs — file written atomically (temp file + replace).
5. `--version` and help must never trigger onboarding.

## Resolved Questions

1. Command naming: **`odi setup` / `odi profile`** (plain language; matches reserved `odi` alias). Copy uses the invoked program name.
2. `current_focus`: **just-in-time only** — not asked on the happy path; asked as the 3rd typed question in the fallback path.

## Builder Calls (made during review)

1. Typed-path fields: schema fields other than `schema_version` are nullable; card renders only non-null lines.
2. `httpx` added as an explicit `cli` package dependency (spec previously, incorrectly, claimed it already was).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy (core)
        run: uv run --directory core mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (mcp_server)
        run: uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (local_server)
        run: uv run --directory local_server mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (cli)
        run: uv run --directory cli mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (client)
        run: uv run --directory client mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (connectors)
        run: uv run --directory connectors mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest (core)
        run: uv run --directory core pytest --cov=core --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.core

      - name: Pytest (mcp_server)
        run: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest --cov=mcp_server --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.mcp_server

      - name: Pytest (local_server)
        run: uv run --directory local_server pytest --cov=local_server --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.local_server

      - name: Pytest (cli)
        run: uv run --directory cli pytest --cov=cli --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.cli

      - name: Pytest (client)
        run: uv run --directory client pytest --cov=client --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.client

      - name: Pytest (connectors)
        run: uv run --directory connectors pytest --cov=connectors --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.connectors

      - name: Combine and report coverage
        run: |
          unset COVERAGE_FILE
          uv run coverage combine \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.core" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.mcp_server" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.local_server" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.cli" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.client" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.connectors"
          uv run coverage xml -o "${{ github.workspace }}/coverage.xml"
          uv run coverage report

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: python -m client.run brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python -m client.run > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:8501 &&
              curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "client.run did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"
